issue_paraphrase: Unpacking the result of a call into multiple assignment targets, like `a, b = f(...)`, makes mypy abort the entire check with an INTERNAL ERROR whenever the called function is overloaded and the assignment context selects an overload whose return type is not a plain tuple. A small standalone module that assigns the unpacked result gets no diagnostics at all: the whole type-check run crashes instead of reporting the real incompatibility in the assignment. The crash happens regardless of how the rest of the file is written.
fix_summary: In check_multi_assignment_from_tuple, the code asserted that the call's reinferred rvalue type is always a TupleType. The fix removes the assertion and, when the context selects an overload whose inferred return type is not a tuple, re-infers the rvalue in an empty context so unpacking still type-checks correctly. Two regression cases cover a call reinferred as a homogeneous tuple and as a non-tuple.
notes: Fast (~2s CLI, ~3.5s golden pytest run) and fully offline; typeshed is vendored under mypy/typeshed so no submodule init is needed. Run mypy as 'python3 -m mypy' from the repo root; no need to pip-install mypy itself. ALWAYS pass --no-incremental --cache-dir to keep the source tree clean. mypy of this era imports librt+ast-serialize at module load (via mypy/nativeparse.py), so those wheels must be installed or mypy fails to start; both have cp312 manylinux wheels. Golden test needs pytest and pytest-xdist (conftest auto-uses xdist); -k filtering makes each run ~3.5s even though full testcheck collection parses all .test files.

issue_paraphrase: With the --allow-redefinition flag enabled, mypy crashes with an internal error on code that is otherwise completely ordinary: a module-level variable initialized to an empty list combined with a function that refers to that same name through a 'global' declaration. Instead of the usual 'need type annotation' hint about the unannotated empty list, the whole type-check run aborts with an INTERNAL ERROR, so no diagnostics of any kind are produced. The crash is triggered by the mere presence of the global statement inside the function.
fix_summary: When propagating names from a scope into the binder, mypy unconditionally called assign_type with the raw symbol type, which for a partial type (empty list literal) crashed. The fix reads the declaration type via get_declaration() and only assigns the binder when a real type exists, filtering out partial types. Regression tests cover both the crash case and a sibling reveal case.
notes: Fast (~2s CLI, ~3.5s golden pytest run) and fully offline. Requires --allow-redefinition on the command line for the CLI repro; the golden .test case sets it via '# flags: --allow-redefinition' inside the test-data file, so the pytest path needs no extra flags. mypy of this era imports librt+ast-serialize at import time; install those wheels (cp312 manylinux available). issue_paraphrase: Inside a runtime membership test such as `if color not in counts:` where counts is an ordinary dict and color is an enum member, mypy wrongly concludes the branch is unreachable and, with --warn-unreachable enabled, flags the statements inside the block as 'Statement is unreachable'. The code is in fact perfectly reachable, since a fresh dictionary is empty the first time it is probed. The spurious error vanishes when the same condition is rewritten, for example inside a helper variable, even though the semantics are identical.
fix_summary: Negative narrowing for iterable-membership checks ('x not in container') now only narrows when the container is a tuple whose items are singleton-equality types (e.g. `x not in (None,)`); for general containers the else_map is cleared because the container could be empty. This removes the false 'unreachable' verdict while keeping the sound special case. A regression test class with an enum + dict membership loop was added under --warn-unreachable.
notes: Fast (~2s CLI, ~3.5s golden pytest run) and fully offline. issue_paraphrase: A default argument on a function parameter whose annotation is a TypeVar declared with a list of value types, like `TypeVar("S", B, C)`, is rejected whenever the default's type is exactly one of the permitted values but is not a supertype of the others: mypy reports 'Incompatible default for parameter' even though the default is legal. The same declaration with a default whose type is a supertype passes, so the checker's verdict depends on which of the value types the default happens to be, not on whether it is allowed. Genuinely invalid defaults are still caught.
fix_summary: In _is_subtype, when the right side is a TypeVarType with a non-empty 'values' list and the left side is not itself a TypeVarType, the left is now a subtype of the TypeVar if it is a (proper) subtype of all the values. A regression case asserts that a default of value type C is accepted while a default of the supertype B is rejected.
notes: Fast (~2s CLI, ~3.5s golden pytest run) and fully offline. NOTE the oracle: BOTH directions exit 1; the observable difference is the presence/absence of the false-positive error line — the golden .test case is the cleanest oracle (FAIL at parent, PASS at fix). mypy runtime needs librt+ast-serialize wheels (cp312 available). issue_paraphrase: A constructor called through a parameter that is annotated as the type object of a TypeVar, e.g. `Type[T]`, is rejected by mypy whenever T's bound is a union of classes: every call site reports 'Incompatible return value type (got "Union[A, B]", expected "T")' even though both classes are instantiable with the same arguments. The constructed value's precise type is inferred correctly — mypy itself reveals it as the individual class — but the check against the TypeVar's declared return type fails anyway, so otherwise valid factory functions are littered with errors. The failure appears in both the no-argument and the one-argument call forms.
fix_summary: ExpressionChecker.analyze_type_type_callee handles a Type[T] call by finding the constructor of each possible type; the return types of those constructors must be replaced with the TypeVar instance T. The fix extracts that substitution into replace_type_type_callee_ret_type and makes it recurse into UnionType items (after get_proper_type and .relevant_items()), so a union-bounded TypeVar yields a union of constructors whose return types are all replaced. A regression case asserts the two revealed types and that no errors are raised; a match-statement case in check-python310.test is updated accordingly.
notes: Fast (~2s CLI, ~3.5s golden pytest run) and fully offline. Note the fix also updates an EXPECTED reveal in test-data/unit/check-python310.test (reveal of choice() in the default match arm changes from 'b.One | b.Two' to 'T_Choice`-1'), so overlaying the fix's test files at the parent is the correct golden procedure; at parent only the new case testTypeUsingTypeCConstructorReturnFromTypeVarUnionBound fails. mypy runtime needs librt+ast-serialize wheels (cp312 available). Use -k-filtered pytest runs.
